newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on HRW crop concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on HRW crop concerns.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on Tuesday amid concerns dry weather would damage hard red winter wheat crops in the U.S. Plains, traders said.

"The key thing was missing that storm in Kansas," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "It just formed up a little bit too far east and tracked north and didn't catch where it was dry."
The state Agriculture Statistics Services on Monday said crop condition ratings had fallen in Texas and Oklahoma in the week ended Sunday. The reports cited continued dry weather.
The National Weather Service offered little hope for rain.
The NWS six- to 10-day outlook called for above-normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation across much of the HRW wheat growing region.
The report compounded concerns that flooding in the Ohio River Valley would damage soft red winter wheat and potential floods in the north would delay spring wheat seedings.
Agronomists said Tuesday the HRW wheat crop was in generally good condition but dryness and disease could cause problems in the coming weeks.
Wheat closed five to three cents per bushel higher with May up three at $3.89-1/2.

The export picture was mixed. Bulls cited news South Korea seeks up to 45,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat while bears pointed to reports the Philippines had rejected offers for 23,500 tonnes U.S. wheat due to high prices.

News Algeria relaunched a tender for 75,000 tonnes of wheat for April/May shipment was also seen as supportive. The tender was for optional origin wheat but there was some speculation that Algeria would snub France due to political tensions.
Algeria did not invite France to submit offers in the origial tender launched last week but traders there had speculated Algeria would purchase French wheat from a foreign company.

Technically, the nine-day relative strenth index (RSI) in the May contract was at 65.89 percent and the July was at 70.19 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
On the day, PaineWebber sold 2.5 million bushels July and Iowa Grain bought 1.5 million July, traders said.
In options, LFG bought 200 July $3.60 calls and sold 200 May $3.60 calls at four cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 11,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 11,618 contracts.
